name: Turoe Stone

attributes.attribute: a human-sized carved boulder near Loughrea in Galway
a Celtic site carved in the La Tene style

sources: Harbison, Peter. Pre-Christian Ireland: From the First Settlers to the Early Celts. London: Thames and Hudson, 1988, 158.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Turoe Stone is an Irish mythological site. It stands in a field outside Loughrea, near Galway City. The boulder is human-sized and upright, its top covered with ornate low reliefs. It first stood near a rath called Feerwore and was moved in historical times to its current place. The carving is in the La Tene style, which marks the stone as Celtic. Its purpose is unknown, though four similar pillar stones are found elsewhere in Ireland. Such stones may mark a central point, like the Stone of Divisions on the hill of Uisneach. A replica of the Turoe Stone stands in the National Museum in Dublin.

okr.objective: Record the Irish site of the Turoe Stone.
